title: Boss: The Compiler Gremlin
story: The Gremlin left five mistakes in the shop till. Go's compiler is strict: it refuses to build until every one is fixed. Fix them and the till prints the total.
goal: Make the program compile and print: Total: 20.00
hints: Read the first compile error. Go reports them in order with line numbers: fix the top one, then press Run again.
The five problems: an unused import, an unused variable, a missing return, a loop that goes one step too far, and mixing float64 with int.
socratic: Which line does the first error point to?
Does Go allow an imported package you never use?
What does i <= len(items) do on the last turn?
explain: In one sentence: what did you learn from “Boss: The Compiler Gremlin”?
